correctness.rationale: Exact minimum follows because covering each unary target needs k-1 fixed copies of each alphabet symbol plus the unique joker. At equality, contrasting the two-run target b^(r+1)a^(k-r-1) forces equal counts of all symbols before the joker. If the ordinary prefix were not t-universal, an absent length-t pattern p followed by k-t copies of its last letter would be absent from the host; reversal gives the corresponding suffix statement. The proved shortest-ordinary-universal arch lemma forces each side to split into alphabet permutations. The construction realizes all targets and the joker boundary t makes the k(q!)^(k-1) representations injective. Edge k=1 is explicit. Direct exhaustive and separately implemented matcher checks: 61,609 balanced hosts over 18 parameter pairs, 5,213 positive hosts; 1,625,493 independent matcher comparison pairs. All-parameter reasoning does not depend on computation.

The closest sources give ordinary subsequence arch results, ordinary-word counting, or contiguous exactly-once partial-word coverage. published-finding corpus nearest items on ordinary insertion radius and binary ordinary-universality distribution have different premises and do not dominate the conclusion. Originality is best-knowledge only and no negative search is treated as proof of novelty.

value.rationale: A single wildcard is a standard compact uncertain-symbol mechanism, whereas scattered-subsequence universality is a natural complete-pattern coverage property. The exact optimum length, complete structural classification of all optimal hosts, and exact all-q all-k count answer a motivated infinite-family design problem. The nontrivial boundary rigidity comes from pairwise prefix-balance and absent-pattern obstructions; it is not a mere arithmetic substitution, finite table, or arbitrary slice. The theorem supplies a fully enumerated minimal design space for target-dependent uncertain-symbol pattern coverage.
